answer_text:
Let \(u \in H^{2}(\mathbb{C}P^{n};\mathbb{Z})\cong \mathbb{Z}\) be the standard generator.  The integral cohomology ring of complex projective space is

\[
H^{*}(\mathbb{C}P^{n};\mathbb{Z}) \cong \mathbb{Z}[u]/(u^{n+1}),
\]

where \(\deg u=2\). In particular,

\[
H^{2n}(\mathbb{C}P^{n};\mathbb{Z}) \cong \mathbb{Z}\, u^{n}.
\]

Suppose \(f:S^{2n}\to \mathbb{C}P^{n}\) induces an isomorphism

\[
f^{*}:H^{2n}(\mathbb{C}P^{n};\mathbb{Z})\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }H^{2n}(S^{2n};\mathbb{Z}).
\]

Since both groups are \(\mathbb{Z}\), this means \(f^{*}(u^{n})\) must be a generator of \(H^{2n}(S^{2n};\mathbb{Z})\cong \mathbb{Z}\), so it must be nonzero.

By naturality of the cup product,

\[
f^{*}(u^{n})=(f^{*}u)^{n}.
\]

Now consider \(n>1\). Then

\[
H^{2}(S^{2n};\mathbb{Z})=0,
\]

so \(f^{*}u=0\). Hence

\[
f^{*}(u^{n})=(0)^{n}=0,
\]

which contradicts the requirement that \(f^{*}(u^{n})\) be a generator of \(H^{2n}(S^{2n};\mathbb{Z})\). Therefore no such map exists for \(n>1\).

For \(n=1\), we have \(\mathbb{C}P^{1}\cong S^{2}\), and the identity map

\[
f:S^{2}\to \mathbb{C}P^{1}
\]

induces an isomorphism on \(H^{2}\). Thus \(n=1\) works.

Therefore the only natural number \(n\ge 1\) with the required property is

\[
\boxed{1}.
\]
